newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA JUNE INFLATION SLOWS DOWN TO 2.3 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA JUNE INFLATION SLOWS DOWN TO 2.3 PCT.

text.p: Monthly inflation in Romania
slowed to 2.3 percent in June from 4.3 percent in May, the
National Statistics Board (CNS) said on Tuesday. The final
figure confirmed a government forecast issued on Monday.
Year-on-year inflation rose to 177.4 percent from 174
percent the previous month, with consumer prices climbing to
101.2 percent from December 1996, the CNS said.
Government officials on Monday said the 2.3 percent rate
was in line with previous inflation forecasts, with monthly
rates expected to keep within a range of three to two percent
in the second half of the year.
In February, the centrist government of Prime Minister
Victor Ciorbea launched tough economic reforms, including price
and markets liberalisation.
The government's original 12-month estimate for this year
has already been revised upward to 110 percent from 90 percent
after steep prices rises in March and April.
Analysts said the new target was still too ambitious,
viewing a 130 to 150 percent level as more realistic.
Increased fares for public transport and postal charges
accounted for much of the June increase. But the rate was kept
low by ample supply of farm products, the CNS said.
